newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik officials say rebel army colonel takes town.
newsitem.headline: Tajik officials say rebel army colonel takes town.

text.p: A rebel colonel has taken control of a large area of southwestern Tajikistan and is demanding changes to a peace deal between the government and the Islamic opposition, Tajik military officials said on Thursday.
"Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev said today that he controls the town of Kurgan Tyube and the adjoining area," a senior Tajik military official told Reuters in the capital Dushanbe.
The government of the former Soviet republic and the Islamic opposition signed a peace deal last month to end a four-year civil war.

"Khudoyberdyev said he still backs the president and the government and is ready to take part in the process of national reconciliation but demands that some points in the peace agreement with the opposition be revised," the official said.
Khudoyberdyev is the head of an elite armoured brigade based in Kurgan Tyube which has about 1,500 servicemen backed by tanks and armoured personnel carriers, the official said.
He said Khudoyberdyev strongly opposed the return of 460 armed Islamic guerrillas to Dushanbe.
The guerrillas are due to return to the capital soon under last month's peace agreement, which provides for opposition participation in all power structures and for new parliamentary elections.

A military official said there was no shooting or disorder in Kurgan Tyube, which is the 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Dushanbe. Khudoyberdyev administrative centre of the Khatlon region and is 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Dushanbe. Khudoyberdyev could not be reached for comment.

The final peace deal, brokered by Russia, Iran and the United Nations and signed by President Imomali Rakhmonov and the Central Asian state's Islamist opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri, ended a civil war in which tens of thousands of people were killed and many more wee driven from their homes.

Under the agreement, 460 Islamist guerrillas should enter Dushanbe soon to safeguard the lives of those opposition members who will work alongside their former opponents from the government and the security ministries.
The latest move by Khudoyberdeyev, a member of the Popular Front set up by the government in 1992 to fight the opposition, follows a power hiatus in the Kurgan Tyube region.
More than two months ago Khudoyberdyev ousted pro-Rakhmonov regional leader Dovlat Sharipov, accusing him of mismanagement.
Power in Kurgan Tyube is said to be held now by a Defence Council set up by Khudoyberdyev last Friday and headed by parliamentary member Shirali Mirzoyev.
Tajik officials told Reuters Rakhmonov had held an urgent meeting of the government and the Popular Front on Wednesday, discussing the situation around Kurgan Tyube.
The rebel colonel could also be trying to reinforce his influence over the region, which has a large aluminium smelter and cotton plantations.

"This is rather Khudoyberdyev's fear of losing his sphere of influence since the situation has become relatively stable after the peace accord that was signed recently," a representative of an international organisation in Tajikistan told Reuters.
In a similar show of force in February, Khudoyberdyev seized the area around the aluminium smelter in the nearby town of Tursunzade but retreated later after talks with the government.
